name: community
description: Community hook templates for the BB Hooks plugin: notifications, integrations, agent automation, and gate policies.
author: MacHatter1

templates.name: Pushover notification
templates.summary: Push to your phone through Pushover.
templates.description: Sends a Pushover push with the thread title and the last reply or error. Create an application at pushover.net to get an API token; your user key is on the dashboard. Both are stored encrypted.
templates.author: MacHatter1

templates.name: Home Assistant webhook
templates.summary: Trigger a Home Assistant automation, for example turn a lamp red when an agent needs you.
templates.description: Posts a small JSON payload to a Home Assistant webhook trigger. Create an automation with a Webhook trigger, copy its URL, and use the event field in your automation's conditions (interaction.pending, thread.idle, …).
templates.author: MacHatter1

templates.name: PagerDuty alert
templates.summary: Trigger a PagerDuty incident when a thread or turn fails.
templates.description: Uses the PagerDuty Events API v2 with an Events integration routing key. Incidents are deduplicated per thread. Severity is one of critical, error, warning, info.
templates.author: MacHatter1

templates.name: Microsoft Teams message
templates.summary: Post to a Teams channel through an incoming webhook or workflow URL.
templates.author: MacHatter1

templates.name: Mattermost message
templates.summary: Post to a Mattermost channel through an incoming webhook.
templates.author: MacHatter1

templates.name: Email via Resend
templates.summary: Email yourself the result or error of a thread through the Resend API.
templates.description: Sends a plain-text email with the last assistant reply or the error. Needs a Resend API key and a verified sender. The key is sent as a bearer token and stored encrypted.
templates.author: MacHatter1

params.label: From address
params.description: A sender on a domain verified in Resend.

templates.name: Comment on the linked GitHub issue
templates.summary: When a thread whose title mentions #123 finishes, post its output as a comment on issue 123.
templates.description: Extracts the first #number from the thread title and posts the thread's final output as an issue comment with the gh CLI. Threads without a #number are ignored.
templates.author: MacHatter1
templates.command:
repo={{repo}}
n=$(printf '%s' "$BB_THREAD_TITLE" | sed -n 's/.*#\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
[ -z "$n" ] && exit 0
body=$("${BB_CLI:-bb}" thread output "$BB_THREAD_ID" 2>/dev/null | head -c 60000)
[ -z "$body" ] && exit 0
printf '%s\n\n_Posted by BB hooks from thread %s._\n' "$body" "$BB_THREAD_ID" | gh issue comment "$n" -R "$repo" --body-file -
templates.notes: Needs the gh CLI authenticated on the machine running the BB server.

templates.name: Archive finished threads
templates.summary: Archive a thread as soon as it goes idle. Scope it with a title filter so only throwaway threads are archived.
templates.author: MacHatter1
templates.notes: Combine with --title '^chore' or a project filter. Archived threads can be unarchived from the sidebar.

templates.name: Provider failover on rate limits
templates.summary: When a turn fails because the provider is rate limited, re-run the same prompt on another provider.
templates.description: Listens to turn.failed, checks that the failure is a rate limit, fetches the thread's latest prompt, and spawns a new thread on the agent you choose in the same workspace, parented to the failed thread. Only top-level threads trigger it, so it never loops.
templates.author: MacHatter1

params.label: Fallback agent
params.description: Which provider (and model) re-runs the prompt when the original is rate limited.

templates.command:
mode={{agent.mode}}; provider={{agent.providerId}}; model={{agent.model}}; reasoning={{agent.reasoningLevel}}; tier={{agent.serviceTier}}
bb="${BB_CLI:-bb}"
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "failover needs jq on the BB server" >&2; exit 1; }
input=$(cat)
category=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.errorInfo.category // empty')
[ "$category" = "rate-limit" ] || exit 0
# Never chain from a thread this hook spawned.
[ -n "$BB_PARENT_THREAD_ID" ] && exit 0
prompt=$("$bb" thread history "$BB_THREAD_ID" --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.[0].input[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text' | head -c 20000)
[ -z "$prompt" ] && exit 0
set -- --project "$BB_PROJECT_ID" --parent-thread "$BB_THREAD_ID"
# A fallback that inherits would hit the same limit; "inherit" here still re-runs on the same provider by request.
if [ "$mode" = "inherit" ]; then provider="$BB_PROVIDER_ID"; model="$BB_MODEL"; reasoning="$BB_REASONING_LEVEL"; tier="$BB_SERVICE_TIER"; fi
[ -n "$provider" ] && set -- "$@" --provider "$provider"
[ -n "$model" ] && set -- "$@" --model "$model"
[ -n "$reasoning" ] && [ "$reasoning" != "none" ] && set -- "$@" --reasoning-level "$reasoning"
[ -n "$tier" ] && set -- "$@" --service-tier "$tier"
[ -n "$BB_ENVIRONMENT_ID" ] && set -- "$@" --environment "$BB_ENVIRONMENT_ID"
"$bb" thread spawn "$@" --prompt "$prompt"
templates.notes: Needs jq and the bb CLI on the machine running the BB server.

templates.name: Continue after capacity errors
templates.summary: Send a continue prompt when a turn fails with a model-capacity error.
templates.description: Checks the failed-turn payload, then the thread's latest provider error. Sends at most one follow-up prompt per thread every two minutes to prevent retry loops.
templates.author: MacHatter1
templates.command:
needle='The model is currently at capacity due to high demand'
if ! jq -e --arg needle "$needle" 'any(.. | strings; contains($needle))' >/dev/null; then
  bb="${BB_CLI:-bb}"
  "$bb" thread log "$BB_THREAD_ID" --json --all 2>/dev/null |
    jq -e --arg needle "$needle" '[.[] | select(.type == "provider/error")] | last // {} | any(.. | strings; contains($needle))' >/dev/null || exit 0
fi
stamp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bb-capacity-continue-${BB_THREAD_ID}"
now=$(date +%s)
last=$(cat "$stamp" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if ! [ "$last" -ge 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then last=0; fi
if [ "$((now - last))" -lt 120 ]; then exit 0; fi
printf "%s\n" "$now" > "$stamp"
"$bb" thread tell "$BB_THREAD_ID" "Continue from where you left off. The previous attempt hit temporary model capacity; do not repeat completed work."
templates.notes: Needs jq and the bb CLI on the machine running the BB server. Checks the latest provider/error log entry when the event omits details.

templates.name: Block messages that contain credentials
templates.summary: Reject any message that looks like it contains an API key, token, or private key.
templates.description: A gate hook with a pattern for common credential shapes: OpenAI, GitHub, AWS, Slack tokens and PEM private keys. Adjust the pattern to your own key formats.
templates.author: MacHatter1

params.label: Reason shown to the sender
params.default: This message looks like it contains a credential. Remove it before sending.

templates.name: Require a ticket reference
templates.summary: Reject a thread's first message unless it references a ticket like ENG-123.
templates.description: Checks only the first message of a thread (later messages pass). The pattern is an extended regular expression tested with grep -E on the BB server.
templates.author: MacHatter1

params.label: Reason shown to the sender
params.default: Start the thread with a ticket reference like ENG-123.

templates.command:
pattern={{pattern}}; message={{message}}
# Only the first message of a thread (status pending) needs a reference.
[ "$BB_THREAD_STATUS" = "pending" ] || exit 0
printf '%s' "$BB_MESSAGE_TEXT" | grep -Eq "$pattern" && exit 0
echo "$message" >&2
exit 2

templates.author: MacHatter1
templates.description: Chains agents: when a thread finishes, a new thread starts in the same workspace with your prompt plus the finished thread's output. Only top-level threads trigger it, so the chain stops after one hop. Scope it with --title or --project.
templates.name: Spawn a follow-up thread
templates.summary: When a thread finishes, start a new thread in the same workspace with your prompt plus the finished thread's output.

params.label: Who runs it
params.description: Same provider and model as the finished thread, or pick one.

templates.command:
prompt={{prompt}}
mode={{agent.mode}}; provider={{agent.providerId}}; model={{agent.model}}; reasoning={{agent.reasoningLevel}}; tier={{agent.serviceTier}}
bb="${BB_CLI:-bb}"
# Only top-level threads chain, so a follow-up never triggers another follow-up.
[ -n "$BB_PARENT_THREAD_ID" ] && exit 0
output=$("$bb" thread output "$BB_THREAD_ID" 2>/dev/null | head -c 20000)
set -- --project "$BB_PROJECT_ID" --parent-thread "$BB_THREAD_ID"
[ -n "$BB_ENVIRONMENT_ID" ] && set -- "$@" --environment "$BB_ENVIRONMENT_ID"
# "inherit" reuses the triggering thread's provider, model and reasoning (BB_MODEL etc. come from the plugin).
if [ "$mode" = "inherit" ]; then provider="$BB_PROVIDER_ID"; model="$BB_MODEL"; reasoning="$BB_REASONING_LEVEL"; tier="$BB_SERVICE_TIER"; fi
[ -n "$provider" ] && set -- "$@" --provider "$provider"
[ -n "$model" ] && set -- "$@" --model "$model"
[ -n "$reasoning" ] && [ "$reasoning" != "none" ] && set -- "$@" --reasoning-level "$reasoning"
[ -n "$tier" ] && set -- "$@" --service-tier "$tier"
"$bb" thread spawn "$@" --prompt "$(printf '%s\n\n---\nOutput of thread %s:\n%s' "$prompt" "$BB_THREAD_ID" "$output")"
templates.notes: Uses the bb CLI from the server (BB_CLI). Only top-level threads trigger it, so chains stop after one hop. Add --title or --project filters to scope it.

templates.author: MacHatter1
templates.description: A guardrail on outgoing messages: anything matching the pattern is rejected before it reaches the agent, and the sender sees your reason. Send now on a queued message can override it.
templates.name: Block messages matching a pattern

params.label: Regular expression

templates.author: MacHatter1
templates.description: Holds messages sent outside the window and sends them automatically when it opens, using the server's local time. Combine with --text '#overnight' to queue only tagged work for the night.
templates.name: Office hours
templates.summary: Hold messages sent outside a daily window until it opens (server local time).
templates.command:
start={{start}}; end={{end}}
now=$(date +%s); h=$(date +%H); m=$(date +%M); s=$(date +%S)
h=${h#0}; m=${m#0}; s=${s#0}
today=$(( h * 3600 + m * 60 + s ))
open=$(( start * 3600 )); close=$(( end * 3600 ))
if [ "$today" -ge "$open" ] && [ "$today" -lt "$close" ]; then exit 0; fi
if [ "$today" -lt "$open" ]; then wait=$(( open - today )); else wait=$(( 86400 - today + open )); fi
printf '{"action":"wait","reason":"Outside office hours (%02d:00-%02d:00)","sendAt":%d}\n' "$start" "$end" $(( (now + wait) * 1000 ))
templates.notes: Combine with --text '#overnight' to hold only tagged messages. Send now on the queued card overrides it.
